title: A week in New York
summary: Seven days of museums and delis, bridges and harbor ferries, Central Park and the High Line, across Manhattan and Brooklyn.
author: Nate Bird

places.name: The Plaza
places.notes: The 1907 landmark on Central Park South. Have tea in the Palm Court even if you don't stay.

places.name: The Standard, High Line
places.notes: Floor-to-ceiling windows straddling the High Line, with river or skyline views.

places.name: Arlo SoHo
places.notes: Small, smart rooms at a fair price, between SoHo and Tribeca.

places.name: Wythe Hotel
places.notes: A 1901 factory turned hotel in Williamsburg, with a rooftop bar facing Manhattan.

places.name: Pod Times Square
places.notes: Tiny, clever rooms near the theaters. The budget pick, with a rooftop.

places.name: Katz's Delicatessen
places.address: 205 E Houston St, New York, NY 10002
places.notes: Pastrami on rye since 1888. Keep your ticket, and tip the carver for a taste.

places.name: Russ & Daughters
places.address: 179 E Houston St, New York, NY 10002
places.notes: Smoked fish and bagels from a family shop open since 1914. Take a number.

places.name: Joe's Pizza
places.notes: The classic New York slice, folded and eaten standing up.

places.name: Nom Wah Tea Parlor
places.notes: Dim sum on Chinatown's crooked Doyers Street since 1920.

places.name: Xi'an Famous Foods
places.notes: Hand-pulled noodles with spicy cumin lamb. Cheap and fiery.

places.name: Veselka
places.notes: Ukrainian pierogi and borscht, open late, in the East Village since 1954.

places.name: Gramercy Tavern
places.notes: Seasonal American cooking. The front tavern room takes walk-ins.

places.name: Grand Central Oyster Bar
places.notes: Oysters and pan roasts under the tiled vaults of Grand Central since 1913.

places.name: Chelsea Market
places.notes: A food hall in the old Nabisco factory. Tacos, lobster and doughnuts before a High Line walk.

places.name: Barney Greengrass
places.notes: The Sturgeon King since 1908. Eggs with lox and onions for a weekend breakfast.

places.name: Levain Bakery
places.notes: Six-ounce chocolate chip walnut cookies, warm from the oven. One is plenty for two.

places.name: Sylvia's Restaurant
places.address: 328 Malcolm X Blvd, New York, NY 10027
places.notes: Harlem's soul food landmark since 1962. Fried chicken and waffles, and a gospel brunch on Sundays.

places.name: Peter Luger Steak House
places.notes: Porterhouse for two and creamed spinach since 1887. Book well ahead.

places.name: Di Fara Pizza
places.notes: A Brooklyn pizza legend, worth the subway ride and the wait.

places.name: McSorley's Old Ale House
places.notes: Light or dark ale, sawdust on the floor and history on every wall since 1854.

places.name: Bemelmans Bar
places.notes: Live piano and murals by the author of Madeline, in the Carlyle Hotel.

places.name: The Dead Rabbit
places.notes: An Irish pub downstairs and award-winning cocktails upstairs, near the Staten Island ferry.

places.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
places.notes: Plan for a full day, or pick two wings. The rooftop garden is open in summer.

places.name: The Museum of Modern Art
places.notes: Van Gogh's Starry Night, Monet's water lilies and much more. Book a timed ticket.

places.name: Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum
places.notes: Frank Lloyd Wright's spiral. Ride to the top and walk down the ramp.

places.name: American Museum of Natural History
places.address: 200 Central Park W, New York, NY 10024
places.notes: Dinosaurs, the blue whale and the planetarium, right on Central Park.

places.name: Whitney Museum of American Art
places.notes: American art with terraces over the Hudson, at the south end of the High Line.

places.name: Tenement Museum
places.notes: Guided tours of real immigrant apartments. Book ahead, then eat at Katz's.

places.name: 9/11 Memorial & Museum
places.notes: The reflecting pools are free. Give the museum a few quiet hours.

places.name: Statue of Liberty
places.notes: Book the ferry from Battery Park early, with pedestal or crown tickets, and include Ellis Island.

places.name: Staten Island Ferry
places.notes: A free harbor cruise past the Statue of Liberty. Stand on the right side going out.

places.name: Empire State Building
places.notes: The 86th-floor open-air deck. Go late at night for fewer people and city lights.

places.name: Top of the Rock
places.notes: The best view of the Empire State Building, with Central Park on the other side.

places.name: Grand Central Terminal
places.notes: Look up at the starry ceiling, and try the whispering gallery by the Oyster Bar.

places.name: New York Public Library
places.notes: The Rose Main Reading Room, guarded by the lions Patience and Fortitude. Free.

places.name: The Met Cloisters
places.address: 99 Margaret Corbin Dr, New York, NY 10040
places.notes: Medieval art in a reassembled monastery high above the Hudson. The unicorn tapestries are the star.

places.name: Apollo Theater
places.notes: Ella Fitzgerald started here. Wednesday's Amateur Night is still a show.

places.name: Brooklyn Museum
places.notes: Egyptian art and Judy Chicago's Dinner Party. The Botanic Garden is next door.

places.name: Central Park
places.notes: Walk from the Pond to Bethesda Terrace and the Ramble, or rent a rowboat at the Loeb Boathouse.

places.name: The High Line
places.notes: An old freight line turned garden walk. Start at Gansevoort St and head north to Hudson Yards.

places.name: Brooklyn Bridge
places.notes: Walk across from Brooklyn toward Manhattan for the skyline. Early morning is quietest.

places.name: Brooklyn Bridge Park
places.notes: Piers turned parks along the East River, with Jane's Carousel and the best Manhattan view.

places.name: Little Island
places.address: Pier 55, Hudson River Park, New York, NY 10014
places.notes: A garden floating on tulip-shaped pillars in the Hudson. Lovely at sunset.

places.name: Washington Square Park
places.notes: The arch, the fountain, street musicians and chess players. The heart of the Village.

places.name: Bryant Park
places.notes: A green lawn behind the library, with an ice rink and holiday market in winter.

places.name: Prospect Park
places.notes: Olmsted's Brooklyn masterpiece, quieter than Central Park. Walk the Long Meadow and around the lake.
